effect: Sudden death: in Battle Mode the hurry-up blocks never stop and fill the whole arena
note: Index 10 sets $1C68 = $FFFF and returns to the title. Normally the block list stops at its $FE marker after 80 blocks, the two outer rings ($C0:D60C); with the flag it runs on through all 143 cells (watched to 122 in Mesen). Lasts until reset. Caravan: the password is accepted but its battle code clears the flag every frame, so nothing happens (Mesen, see the Caravan hurry-up card).

code: X turbo on pad 1 at the title menu
effect: Battle stages 11 (boxing ring) and 12 (trampolines) on the stage select
note: $CC:14C0: 48 X presses in a row, each 7-9 frames after the last (49 presses; about 6.5 s at 8 frames), set $1CB5 and play sound $0D (the jingle GameFAQs mentions). Any turbo pad or fast tapping works, not just the Joycard. 6 or 10 frames apart fails. The Caravan version clears $1CB5 at the stage select, so it never works there.

code: A or START on multitap pad 5 at the title menu
effect: Battle Mode: Y jumps, in every stage except 2 and 3
note: $CC:13B0 sets $1C6E when the pad 5 press that chooses any menu item is A or START. $C0:65F1 then allows the jump everywhere but battle stages 2 and 3 (without the flag, only stage 12 has it). Lasts until reset. Checked with an emulated multitap in port 2 (Mesen), A on multitap port D: $1C6E = $FFFF in all five versions; A on pad 4 or pad 1 leaves it 0.

code: SELECT on the battle player screen
effect: Change that player's colour
note: $CC:2152: each of pads 1-4 cycles its own colour $1CB7/$1CB9/$1CBB/$1CBD through 15 values. Colours another player already has are skipped.

effect: In-game debug menu: press SELECT in Normal Game (STAGE NO. warp incl. 6-0 ending, NO DEATH, FIRE 0-9, BOMB 1-9, BOMB TYPE 0/1/2/4/8, ITEM FULL)
note: Flips the disabled switch at $C1:5B40. Same byte as patches/sb2_debug_menu_<ver>.ips (ROM offset $15B40 = 01). Up/Down picks a line (wraps over 9 lines), Right/Left steps the value, START closes it (and pauses; START again to play). NO DEATH sets 144 hearts, which never decrease ($C0:A644 only takes hearts below $80). BOMB TYPE 4 = spike bomb (burns through soft blocks), 8 = an unnamed fifth type. The last three lines (-) do nothing. Every line checked on the patched ROMs in Mesen. The Game Genie code patches the same ROM byte.

effect: Stages 11 and 12 on the battle stage select without the Joycard trick
note: Disabled switch at $CC:239F (LDA #0 / BNE) that skips the $1CB5 check. Europe: CC23FC01, Japan: CC239001. Caravan has its own switch at $CC:250E: CC251001 (checked in Mesen: 12 stages, Left 1 -> 12 -> 11). The Game Genie code patches the same ROM byte. Europe CC23FC01 and Japan CC239001 (the high byte of the same LDA #0, so A is $0100) entered in Mesen's cheat engine: $7F:401E = 11 and Left on the stage select goes 1 -> 12 in both.

effect: Caravan version: stages 11 and 12 on the battle stage select (the event build otherwise allows 4)
note: Disabled switch at $CC:250E (LDA #0 / BNE to $CC:2527) that skips the 4-stage limit and the $1CB5 clear. Checked with Mesen's cheat engine: $7F:401E = 11 instead of 3, Left on the stage select goes 1 -> 12 -> 11 (without it 1 -> 4 -> 3). The Game Genie code patches the same ROM byte.

effect: CPU usage meter (a black scanline where the frame's work ends)
note: $C1:00BD: force-blank for a few cycles at the end of each frame's work, in both main loops. The Game Genie code patches the same ROM byte.

effect: Jump in Normal Game (Y)
note: $C1:3D26 switch, calls the battle jump code $C0:6616/$C0:6658. The Game Genie code patches the same ROM byte.

effect: Press R in Normal Game for every power-up
note: $C0:22A0: speed 3, 9 bombs, fire 9, remote, kick, glove, both pass items and 144 hearts (checked in RAM). The Game Genie code patches the same ROM byte.

effect: Battle stage 11 / 12
note: $1CCD is the chosen battle stage. Checked with Mesen's cheat engine (USA): the stage select shows 11 / 12 and the battle is the boxing ring / trampolines. Caravan: entered in Mesen's cheat engine, the select shows 11 but the battle loads retail stage 10's forest arena ($1A = $0B), because its stage table maps 10-15 to $0B.

code: BOMB TYPE 4 / 8 in the debug menu
effect: Spike bomb (4): the blast burns through every soft block in range. Type 8: a fifth bomb type that bounces off in random directions when thrown
note: $80F3 values; each has its own item counter ($80E5 type 4, $80E8 type 8) and pickup handler ($C0:9965, $C0:9C19). Type 4 checked in Mesen next to soft blocks; type 8 checked in Mesen (7E80F308 + glove): a thrown type-8 bomb takes a new random direction on its bounces, a type-0 bomb keeps the throw direction; kicking not exercised.

code: SNES Mouse in any port (Europe, Caravan)
effect: The title menu ignores all input while a mouse is plugged in
note: Europe ($CC:1364) and Caravan ($CC:1494) read the controller IDs $CD-$D1 and, on a mouse (AND #$1E = 2), skip the menu. Checked in Mesen with a mouse in port 2: Europe and Caravan stay on the title, USA and Japan work; Caravan with a pad in port 2 plays normally. Image: Caravan with the mouse (left) and with a pad (right).

effect: Player 1 invincible in Normal Game (144 hearts, which never go down)
note: Same value as the debug menu's NO DEATH: a hit takes a heart only below $80. Own bomb in 1-1: he flashed and played on (without the code he died and 1-1 restarted). Game Genie: a hit with no hearts goes to the heart-loss flash instead of dying (JML $C0:A675 at $C0:833C -> $C0:834A, BEQ at $C0:A650 and $C1:4180 -> the flash, JML at $C1:5567 -> $C1:5576); Mesen, all five: own bomb in 1-1, he played on with his kit (without it he died and lost it).

effect: Speed 3, 9 bombs, fire 9 (HUD 10)
note: Player 1 kit $7E:80E0-$80E2; RAM checked after a bomb. No Game Genie form: speed, bombs and fire are read through the player pointer at about 20 places (and copied to +$F0-$F2), and written only at game start, by pickups and by the R switch C022F301 (which gives everything).

effect: Spike bombs (blast through soft blocks); 7E80F301 remote control, 7E80F302 power bomb
note: Bomb type $7E:80F3; 4 checked in RAM, types checked on screen through the debug menu earlier. Game Genie: LDA [$6A],Y -> LDA #$04 at $C0:350B, the type load copied to each new bomb (+$42); Mesen, all five: the bomb laid in 1-1 got type 4 (0 without).

effect: Both pass items, power glove, kick
note: RAM checked; the glove and kick flags are the ones the pickup handlers set. No Game Genie form built: the four items have four separate tests (wall pass $C0:AF6A, bomb pass $C0:AEBC, glove $C0:30E6, kick $C0:63AC), and the PAR check was RAM only.

effect: Battle stages 11 and 12 without the Joycard trick
note: $1CB5 is the flag the turbo-X code sets. Left on the stage select went 1 -> 12. Caravan clears it at the stage select (no effect there). Game Genie: BEQ +7 -> BEQ +0 after LDA $001CB5 ($CC:23AF; EU $CC:240A, JP $CC:239E), so the stage count is always 12; Mesen, USA, Europe, Japan, beta: Left on the stage select went 1 -> 12.

effect: Jump (Y) in every battle stage but 2 and 3
note: $1C6E, the flag the pad-5 trick sets. The cheat engine held it at $FFFF; the jump itself was checked with the real pad-5 trick (same flag). Game Genie: BEQ -> BEQ +0 after LDA $001C6E ($C0:65F5); Mesen, all five: the jump handler $C0:6616 runs in battle stage 1 (never without the code).

effect: Sudden death: the hurry-up blocks fill the whole arena (password 5656)
note: $1C68 held at $FFFF by the cheat engine; the effect was checked earlier with the flag set by 5656. Game Genie: BEQ -> BEQ +0 after LDA $001C68 ($C0:D615, Caravan $C0:D624), so the block list never stops at its $FE marker; Mesen (tools/sb2/sudden_death.lua with the flag cleared), USA, Europe, Japan, beta: the blocks kept coming past 81 (control stops at 81). Caravan not run (the test never reaches the hurry-up there).

effect: Unreferenced test code: pad 1 R adds $0400, L subtracts $0200 from each entry of the HDMA scroll tables $7E:393C / $7E:3730 (set up for BG1 by $C0:0EDB from $C5:FD57)
note: $C0:0E9B. No caller and no pointer anywhere; never ran in the coverage logs.

effect: Unreferenced second init entry: force blank, the boot init calls ($C0:209F, $C0:0F2C, $C0:211A, $C0:F60E, $C0:159E, $C0:096C), then a wait loop
note: $C0:0C5F. Looks like an older reset path; nothing jumps to it.

code: CC03E401 or CC03E408, then battle stage 1
effect: Two battle stages the Caravan was thought to have removed: the ice arena (2) and the warp-hedge arena (7)
note: Battle maps its stage number to an internal stage through a 16-byte table at $CC:03E4 (retail 00 01 02 05 06 07 08 09 0A 0B 04 03 ...). The Caravan's reads 00 09 0A 0B 0B ..., so only 4 stages are reachable, and even its 12-stage select code can't get further. Its entry 0 set to 1 or 8 loads retail stage 2 or 7 complete and playable; internal 2-7 (retail 3, 12, 11, 4, 5, 6) load with junk tiles, so their data is gone. Mesen.

code: World 2: password 6442 + CC19C027 C5E0E8A6 C5E0E98F C5E0EAC3
effect: Four unused boss arenas, one per world 2-5, in that world's own tiles and frame
note: Each stage's struct ($C5:DF41 + stage x 3) points at an area layout. Every world has its own eighth layout after area 7 (world 2 $C3:8FA6, 3 $C4:2105, 4 $C4:4A82, 5 $C4:724B), but all five boss stages point at world 1's ($C3:6ACE), so each boss fights in the grey arena. Nothing points at the four. Repointing a boss stage's struct to its world's layout loads it: the arena in that world's tiles and border, and the boss plays as normal (the pillar grid is the same). Codes: CC19C0xx sends the password to area 8 (table $CC:19BE); world 3: 3903 + CC19C237 C5E13005 C5E13121 C5E132C4; world 4: 9564 + CC19C447 C5E17882 C5E1794A C5E17AC4; world 5: 7735 + CC19C657 C5E1C04B C5E1C172 C5E1C2C4. The layouts are the same in all five versions; seen in Mesen (USA). Image: the real 2-8, then worlds 2-5's own arenas.

effect: Eight sound effects the game never plays
note: Effects are queued through $C3:A4B5: immediates before each call, the wrapper $CC:815D (A + $40) and the table $C5:D54E. Together they request 41-45, 47-5F, 61, 64, 66, 68-6A, 6D and 6F-72. 46, 60, 62, 63, 65, 6B, 6C and 6E are never asked for, and each plays: 46 two short high notes, 60 and 62 two-voice hits, 63 a rattle of about 1 s, 65 a rising sweep of about 1.6 s (64 has the same shape but stays low), 6B a figure repeated for about 6 s, 6C about 7 s of pulses, 6E a held tone of about 3.9 s. Recorded in BizHawk at the title with the music stopped.

effect: The hurry-up starts at 0:58 and the blocks at 0:53, stop after the outer rings, then a second wave fills the middle from 0:14; password 5656's sudden death does nothing
note: Caravan $C0:D887-D8E9 and $C0:D600-D60E (retail $C0:D869, $C0:D600; $C1:0B89 CMP #3 -> #5): HURRY UP at 0:58 and blocks at 0:53 (retail 0:38 / 0:33). When the first wave reaches the $FE marker (cell 81) it sets $5D0E bit $80 and waits; at 0:14 the counter $5D12 is reset to $51 and a second wave drops the inner cells. $1C68 (the 5656 sudden-death flag) is cleared every battle frame. Mesen: wave 1 from 0:53, held at 81 until 0:14, then 81 -> 112 by 0:07; $1C68 = 1 read back as 0 within frames. Image: 0:53, 0:15 and 0:07.

effect: A cut battle gimmick: pits open and close in the floor in patterns
note: $C0:3FAD (unreferenced). $C0:3FAD has no reference of any kind. On a timer ($7E:5CCC, flag $7E:5CCE) it picks one of 8 position sets from $C5:E714 at random and starts tile animations from script $C5:E7D3 (tiles $18C0-$18C6, ending as cell type $D6, a hole) or $C5:E7F5 (the reverse, closing it). The per-frame animator $C0:DA53 (717 bytes, list $7E:2860 over the pool $7E:3D88) writes each frame's tile to $7F:A000/$B000 and the cell type to $7F:C000/$D000; nothing else ever adds to that list. Forced in Mesen by pointing the battle stage's handler entry ($C0:3707 + 4 x $1A) at $C0:3FAD for one session: black pits open in a T shape and in pairs. Image: normal (left), then 60 and 900 frames in. Static: Europe, Japan and beta have the routine, the pattern data ($C5:E714, $C5:E7D3), the handler table ($C0:3707) and the animator ($C0:DA53) byte-identical at the same addresses, still unreferenced; Caravan has the same routine and data with the animator moved to $C0:DAB0, but forcing it there showed no pits in 1500 frames, so it is left out.
